decisions.evidence: Overturn render -> models. Sits mid-run in the single contiguous models object file 0x4d4810-0x4d7850; the assigner's own boundaries array records no transition at 0x4d6fc0 or 0x4d7610, so the 'render' label was a 2-function island with no seam. pack.py confirms it shares BOTH globals with its models-labeled bracketing neighbours 0x4d6880 and 0x4d7850 (DAT_0087bc14 model tag table + PTR_sig__matrix4x3_multiply_sig_00696664) - identical global-reference fingerprint means same object file. Body: indexes the model tag at DAT_0087bc14, checks tag group 0x769c097, composes per-node matrix4x3 transforms, selects LOD from the tag's 5 pixel-size thresholds (puVar1[2..6]) with DAT_006893e8 override, packs a node/flags block and hands it to 0x4d72a0; the rasterizer_set_model_skinning / 0x526f50 / 0x52b530 calls are ordinary downstream cross-module calls, not evidence of residence. External callers 0x4924b0 (slice 04) and 0x510c50 (slice 09) invoke it alongside 0x4d53f0/0x4d7610/0x4d7690/0x4d7850, all models. Caveat: the run label 'models' itself is only ~0.45 confidence (could be a render_model/object-render file); if the run is later relabelled these two must move with it.

Overturn render -> models, same reasoning and same run. Sole caller is 0x4d6fc0 (immediately preceding) and it is immediately followed by models-labeled 0x4d7610, so it cannot be a separate object file without inventing two seams the boundaries array does not have. pack.py: receives the model tag pointer as param_1 and walks its region/permutation/geometry-part tables (offsets 0xc4/0xc8/0xd4/0xe0), transforming part bounds via matrix4x3_transform_point before calling rasterizer_set_up_node_parts - model-geometry traversal that calls out to the rasterizer, not rasterizer/render code. Also references DAT_0087bc14, the same model tag table anchoring the run.
